summary: Fourteen days of Nightscout data with 98.7 percent CGM coverage at 5-minute cadence, 3995 valid entries, no invalid or duplicate readings, and a largest gap of 65 minutes. Aggregate metrics are mean 121.6 mg/dL, standard deviation 39.7, coefficient of variation 32.6 percent, time in range 86.0 percent, time above range 8.9 percent, time below range 5.1 percent. The dominant pattern is a daily oscillation rather than a stable offset: local hours 12:00 to 17:00 rise to a peak at 16:00 (mean 162.8 mg/dL, 32.1 percent above range) and local hours 18:00 to 19:00 and 22:00 to 03:00 carry the hypoglycemia burden (15.3 percent below range at 19:00, 18.5 percent at 01:00), with level 2 lows of 42, 41 and 42 mg/dL. Zero carbohydrate entries were recorded over the entire period and cob was 0 in every sampled loop status, so all meal coverage runs through the UAM path. Loop reason strings show that configured SMB minute caps form only the base of the dose and are then multiplied by build-specific boost factors, with a nominal cap near 0.167 U producing a delivered SMB of 1.6 U during one high-glucose episode. Insulin on board reached 5.935 U against a configured ceiling of 25 U that never bound, and effective sensitivity from dynamic ISF ranged from 27.8 to 124.0 mg/dL/U against a flat profile ISF of 56 mg/dL/U. The early-morning window from 04:00 to 08:00 local is clean and stable, which supports current basal magnitude in those segments.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM data is sufficient for all downstream stages: 3995 of 4046 expected entries, 98.7 percent coverage, 5-minute cadence, zero invalid, zero duplicate, zero out-of-period readings, 10 gaps with a largest of 65 minutes. Local time is unambiguous (BST, +60 minutes, device-sourced) and hourly_glucose_local hour h equals hourly_glucose hour h-1 throughout, verified at local 00:00 (93.3 mg/dL) and local 16:00 (162.8 mg/dL). Boundary days 2026-08-07 (33 readings) and 2026-08-21 (269 readings) are partial and excluded from day-level comparison. All 17 profile inventory items are present with values; profile basal totals 16.2 U/day, matching the profile switch label naming 16-2u per day, which corroborates that the selected profile ran during the period. Carbohydrate telemetry is empty: carb_entries 0, total_carbs_g 0.0, carb_treatment_entries empty, extended_carb_entries 0. Insulin totals are 655 entries and 275.95 U, about 19.7 U/day of bolus and SMB, with delivered temp basal volume not quantified, so total daily dose can only be bracketed near 30 to 36 U/day. The period is not stationary: profile switch on 08-13, site changes on 08-10, 08-13 and 08-17, sensor changes on 08-11 and 08-21, occlusion and pump error on 08-19, and GLP-1 1.25 mg on 08-14, 08-17 and 08-20. Mean glucose was near 114 mg/dL for 08-08 to 08-12 and near 126 mg/dL for 08-13 to 08-21. The loop is a customized AAPS variant containing Enhanced oref1, UAM Boost 1 and 2, UAM High Boost, G3 pre-UAM uncertainty hold, prTrial, twin and antBackout fields, so standard reasoning transfers only partially.

Exercise and hypoglycemia rescue treatments are absent. u200 dilution handling appears only in a free-text note.

analysis_steps.findings: Time below range of 5.1 percent exceeds the common reference of under 4 percent and is the binding constraint on every later stage, while coefficient of variation 32.6 percent and time in range 86.0 percent are within common targets. Level 2 hypoglycemia clusters on 08-13 near 18:00 to 18:14 UTC (51, 47, 42, 45 mg/dL), 08-14 near 18:04 to 18:14 UTC (48, 41, 41 mg/dL) and 08-21 at 06:19 UTC (42 mg/dL). Hypoglycemia concentrates in two local windows: 18:00 and 19:00 (7.7 and 15.3 percent below range) and 22:00 through 03:00 (6.6, 10.1, 11.4, 18.5, 10.1 and 10.2 percent). Hyperglycemia is a single afternoon block from local 13:00 to 17:00 peaking at 16:00, plus a secondary local 10:00 peak (mean 148.0, 20.2 percent above range). Worst days combine both extremes: 08-18 (71.9 percent in range, 12.8 percent below), 08-14 (70.8 percent in range, 8.3 percent below). Correction response windows show descents far larger than the logged dose can explain: 0.2 U at 234 mg/dL fell 178 mg/dL in 120 minutes on 08-14; 0.65 U at 264 mg/dL fell 168 mg/dL on 08-19; 0.2 U at 172 mg/dL fell 125 mg/dL by 240 minutes on 08-13. Loop states corroborate stacking: IOB 4.73 U with variable_sens 37.9 and SMB 1.6 U on 08-19, and IOB 5.935 U with variable_sens 27.8 and insulin_req 2.12 on 08-21. Predicted minGuardBG reached minus 4 on 08-11 and minus 59 on 08-16 before 120-minute zero temps were issued, meaning the controller detects overshoot only after delivery. Confounders that must not be attributed to settings include the occlusion and pump error at 08-19 13:40 UTC preceding the 264 mg/dL peak, the site change on 08-17 preceding the worst day 08-18, and the sensor change on 08-21 at 09:08 UTC occurring about 2.8 hours after the 42 mg/dL low, which makes end-of-session inaccuracy a live alternative explanation for that single event.

analysis_steps.findings: The only window plausibly free of both meals and residual correction insulin, local 04:00 to 08:00, is stable and well controlled: means 106.0, 104.2, 99.5 and 99.5 mg/dL, time in range 95.8, 95.2, 97.5 and 98.7 percent, below range 3.0, 4.8, 2.5 and 1.3 percent, with no time above range, against basal 0.6 rising to 0.7 at 05:00 and 0.8 at 06:00 U/h. This is the strongest available evidence that basal magnitude in those segments is broadly appropriate. From 22:00 to 03:00 local the hourly means remain normal (105.7, 93.3, 90.6, 101.9, 104.7 mg/dL) while below-range time is high, which is the signature of residual insulin action rather than an excessive baseline rate, since a genuinely over-set basal would depress the mean as well. The profile shape does look phase-shifted relative to observation, with the lowest daytime basal of 0.5 U/h at 16:00 coinciding with the highest hourly mean of the day, and basal rising to 0.6 at 18:00 and 0.7 at 19:00 into the highest hypoglycemia hour. That shape observation is not converted into a change because unannounced meals, boost-scaled UAM dosing, a 10-hour DIA tail and dynamic ISF remain unseparated explanations, and because repeated 120-minute zero temps in the evening indicate the controller is braking against insulin residue rather than against baseline delivery. Targets cannot be validated as configured: profile targets are 90, 100 from 08:00 and 90 from 23:00 mg/dL, but sampled loop target_bg takes 13 distinct values from 80 to 116 mg/dL, with recurring 80 mg/dL targets during the aggressive high-glucose episodes on 08-10, 08-18, 08-19 and 08-21, while autosens_raises_target and autosens_lowers_target are both false and logged temporary targets explain only part of the spread.

analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carbohydrate log to exclude meals from the 13:00 to 19:00 local block. No exercise log. No per-hour IOB series to test the residual insulin hypothesis directly. The target modulation rule in this custom build is undocumented. Loop rate values are too sparsely sampled to reconstruct delivered basal per hour.

analysis_steps.findings: Carb ratio cannot be validated because no meal was ever declared. The only available check is internal consistency, and loop-reported carb ratios match the profile in the 04:00, 08:00, 16:00 and 20:00 local segments, with a small persistent difference in the 00:00 to 04:00 segment where the loop reports 13.3 g/U against a profile value of 13.0 g/U, seen on 08-16 and 08-19. That roughly 2 percent offset may reflect dynamic carb ratio behavior, profile percentage or unit rounding, and it is recorded as a consistency observation rather than a defect. Profile ISF is a single flat 56 mg/dL/U, but dynamic_sensitivity_enabled is true with an adjustment factor of 70 percent and autosens_enabled is false, so operational sensitivity is not the profile value. Sampled variable_sens spans 27.8 to 124.0 mg/dL/U with a median near 79, and the dependence on glucose is monotonic: 27.8 at 245.7 mg/dL, 37.9 at 262.2, 42.5 at 135 with a deviation of 7.1, 43.2 at 171.9, rising to 108.4 at 84 and 124.0 at 69.8. At the afternoon peak the controller therefore assumes insulin is roughly twice as strong as the flat profile anchor and dosed accordingly, with insulin_req of 1.98 to 2.59 U and rates driven to the safe ceiling. Because dynamic ISF is anchored to the profile ISF and total daily dose, the flat ISF value and the 70 percent factor cannot be evaluated separately in this package and must not be moved together. DIA is 10 hours with insulin_type free_peak_oref and no peak time supplied. Extended negative effects at 240 and 360 minutes are visible, for example 0.05 U on 08-17 producing minus 34, minus 68 and minus 50 mg/dL at 2, 4 and 6 hours, but every such window is contaminated by subsequent SMB and temp basal activity, so DIA inference is blocked by evidence rather than merely uncertain.

analysis_steps.data_gaps: Insulin peak time. Carbohydrate entries. Any clean isolated bolus decay window. The total daily dose value used internally by dynamic ISF. Confirmation of how u200 dilution is represented.

analysis_steps.findings: All six AAPS groups and all 18 components carry non-null values, so verify is not admissible for any AAPS group and each must resolve to change or keep. SMB and UAM are both enabled and are the only mechanism covering meals, since carbohydrate entries are zero and cob is 0 in every sampled status, so disabling either would remove all coverage of the afternoon excursion block. The activation flags are internally coherent: with smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled false, the frequent 135 mg/dL temporary targets act as a deliberate SMB off-switch, which is a purposeful defensive pattern rather than a defect, while smb_with_cob_enabled false and smb_after_carbs_enabled false are effectively inert under smb_always_enabled true and zero carbohydrate entries. The configured minute caps reconcile exactly with reported standardMaxBolus values: 15 minutes against 0.7 to 0.8 U/h basal gives 0.175 to 0.20 U matching a reported 0.2, and 20 minutes against 0.8 U/h gives 0.267 U matching a reported 0.3. However those caps form only the base of the calculation and are then scaled by UAM Boost 1 between 0.68 and 1.34, UAM Boost 2 between 0.24 and 35.93, an increased SMB percentage path, and a UAM High Boost path. On 08-19 at 15:54 UTC the basal in force was 0.5 U/h, giving a nominal 20-minute base of about 0.167 U, while the reason string states SMB equals 1.6, roughly ten times the nominal base. The effective delivery cap is therefore not the configured minute cap, and this is the mechanism that links configuration to the observed level 2 hypoglycemia. The remaining inconsistency is that max_uam_smb_basal_minutes at 20 exceeds max_smb_basal_minutes at 15, so the less certain unannounced path is permitted a larger base than the announced path that is never used. The 3-minute interval is retained as the configured minimum spacing and was not confused with any remaining-time text in reason strings; no evidence in the package isolates the interval itself as the driver. UAM is treated strictly as unannounced-rise detection and no duplicate COB counting is claimed, since cob is 0 in every sampled status.

analysis_steps.data_gaps: The boost multiplier configuration is not exposed anywhere in the package. Per-event SMB volumes are not itemized, so boosted delivery is inferred from reason strings rather than measured. Gap timestamps are not itemized, so a post-gap delta artifact cannot be excluded as a contributor to isolated boost events.

analysis_steps.findings: The configured max_basal_u_per_hour of 12 U/h is inert. The 08-14 reason string states adj. req. rate 5.9 reduced to maxSafeBasal 4, and with a maximum profile basal of 0.8 U/h the max_daily_safety_multiplier of 5.0 yields exactly 4.0 U/h, which binds below both the 12 U/h setting and the 6.0 current basal safety multiplier path. Changing the 12 U/h value would therefore produce no behavioral effect. The configured max_iob_units of 25 U has never bound: peak observed IOB was 5.935 U on 08-21, then 4.73 U on 08-19, 2.802 U and 2.23 U. Against an estimated total daily dose of 30 to 36 U/day, a 25 U ceiling is roughly 70 to 80 percent of daily dose, so the last-resort brake is functionally absent, and it was absent precisely during the two episodes preceding the 168 and 176 mg/dL descents. Autosens is off while dynamic sensitivity is on, which is a valid non-conflicting single-engine configuration, and both autosens target flags are consistently false. sensitivity_ratio is not stuck at 1: observed values include 0.79, 0.88, 0.91, 0.92, 0.94, 0.98 and 1.0, confirming an active adjustment path where 1 is a neutral current adjustment rather than a disabled feature. The sensitivity group is the strongest candidate mechanism for the crashes, but the 70 percent factor is mathematically anchored to the flat profile ISF of 56 and to total daily dose, so changing it now would alter every dosing decision including the already hypoglycemia-prone overnight window and would permanently confound the profile ISF question. The carbohydrate absorption group has not been exercised once: min_5m_carbimpact and meal_max_absorption_hours govern COB decay and meal modelling, and with zero carbohydrate entries and cob 0 in every status there is no observational basis to move either value. Automation is clearly compensating for ISF, since the profile value is only an anchor and operational sensitivity varies by a factor of more than four. Automation is also modulating targets by an undocumented mechanism, which is a material inconsistency that caps confidence in any target decision. Automation compensates for basal only reactively, and the evening pattern of normal means with high time below range indicates braking against residual insulin rather than an excessive baseline, which weakens the basal shape hypothesis. DIA interacts with stacking but remains evidence-blocked. Carb ratio is not compensated because the carbohydrate path was never invoked.
analysis_steps.evidence: representative_loop_statuses reason string maxSafeBasal 4 on 08-14 and requested rate 4 on 08-21; iob values 5.935, 4.73, 2.802 and 2.23; variable_sens range 27.8 to 124.0; sensitivity_ratio values 0.79 to 1.0; aaps_profile.smb_settings.raw_settings max_iob_units 25, max_basal_u_per_hour 12, max_daily_safety_multiplier 5.0, current_basal_safety_multiplier 6.0, dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent 70, min_5m_carbimpact 8, meal_max_absorption_hours 7; minGuardBG minus 4 on 08-11 and minus 59 on 08-16; treatment_summary carb_entries 0.
analysis_steps.dependencies: safety_overview, basal_targets, profile_cr_isf_dia and automation_smb_uam. The sensitivity group cannot be separated from the profile ISF anchor within this package, so both are held while narrower downstream levers are evaluated.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: The internal total daily dose used by dynamic ISF is not exposed. Loop statuses are sampled at 24 of 6214, so the sensitivity_ratio and variable_sens distributions are indicative rather than complete. The custom target modulation rule is undocumented. Delivered basal volume is not summarized, so the estimated daily dose used to judge the 25 U ceiling is a bracket.

analysis_steps.findings: The user-declared aaps_profile.analysis_context is source declared_by_user with meal_strategies as an empty list, period_exceptions null and strategy_stable_for_period null. There are therefore no declared prebolus_minutes, immediate_bolus_percent or e-carb fields present in the package to reproduce, and because strategy_stable_for_period is null the stability rule cannot be applied to elevate any representative declaration. Observed telemetry is consistent with the empty declaration: 655 insulin entries totalling 275.95 U were delivered with zero declared grams, no Meal Bolus, Bolus Wizard or Carb Correction event type appears in representative_treatments, and every therapy response window is a Correction Bolus with is_extended_carbs false. The de facto strategy is fully reactive, with no prebolus, no immediate bolus fraction, and SMB with UAM carrying all meal coverage. Two recurring rise patterns are visible in local time. The mid-morning pattern runs 09:00 to 11:00 with means climbing 99.5, 110.5, 132.9, 148.0 and 132.3 mg/dL, illustrated by 0.2 U at 100 mg/dL on 08-14 rising 88 mg/dL in 60 minutes and reaching 235 mg/dL at 240 minutes. The afternoon pattern is a broad plateau from 12:00 to 17:00 peaking at 16:00, which is the shape a reactive controller handles worst because there is no discrete onset. The counterpart descent from 16:00 to 19:00 falls from 162.8 to 105.4 mg/dL with 7.7 and 15.3 percent time below range and the two deepest level 2 clusters of the period. Response windows show insulin arriving after the peak and persisting past the fall, for example 0.2 U at 234 mg/dL on 08-14 producing minus 178 mg/dL at 120 minutes and 61 mg/dL still at 360 minutes, which the logged dose alone cannot produce and which matches boost-scaled UAM delivery plus temp basal at the 4 U/h ceiling. Several windows show crash then large rebound, such as 47 mg/dL at 240 minutes followed by 204 mg/dL at 360 minutes on 08-13, and 71 mg/dL at 60 minutes followed by 225 mg/dL at 120 minutes on 08-12, which is consistent with unlogged rescue carbohydrate and means true time below range may be understated while some rebound highs are iatrogenic. Critically, this establishes that a reactive-only strategy explains the oscillation but does not establish that adding prebolus or immediate bolus insulin would be safe, because without a working IOB brake earlier insulin would move the same load earlier rather than reduce it. No prebolus interval and no immediate bolus percentage can be derived from this package, and the observed 60 to 120 minute lag is a property of the reactive loop rather than a measured prebolus requirement.

analysis_steps.data_gaps: No carbohydrate amounts or meal timestamps anywhere in the period. No rescue carbohydrate records to confirm the rebound hypothesis. Meal composition, calculated bolus and any percentage are absent and are not inferred.

analysis_steps.findings: There are zero carbohydrate entries and therefore zero extended carbohydrate entries, so no absorption pattern exists to fit. average_extended_carb_duration_min is a genuine null and is not interpreted, and no e-carb duration is inferred from any aggregate. Assessment of e-carb amount, start offset, duration and observed glucose action time is unavailable rather than partially limited. An AAPS e-carb entry is a carbohydrate declaration spread over a duration that supplies COB so the algorithm can dose proactively, and it is explicitly not a pump extended or dual-wave bolus that spreads insulin delivery; neither appears in the data. This distinction matters because the deficit identified is an information deficit rather than an insulin delivery shape deficit. The two carbohydrate absorption parameters remain entirely unexercised and are held. One forward-looking feasibility check is that the configuration is already compatible with carbohydrate announcement, because smb_always_enabled true means SMB would continue regardless of COB, so smb_with_cob_enabled false and smb_after_carbs_enabled false would not block dosing, and min_carbs_required_grams of 20 would gate only the COB-dependent path. The slow afternoon plateau is, on shape alone, the kind of profile e-carbs are designed for, but that is recorded strictly as a hypothesis for future data because a duration cannot be fitted to zero observations.

analysis_steps.findings: A contradiction audit against aaps_profile, profile_context and decision_inventory was completed and produced four corrections and confirmations. First, profile_context states authoritative_source aaps_profile and historical_applicability yes, so the 08-13 profile switch is retained only as a residual validity caveat and not as grounds to discard the profile; the 16.2 U/day computed basal total matching the switch label supports this. Second, the earlier working hypothesis that afternoon and evening basal shape is defective is downgraded, because normal hourly means with high time below range in the evening and overnight indicate residual insulin rather than an excessive baseline, and because the clean 04:00 to 08:00 local window supports current basal magnitude. Third, verify is not admissible for any AAPS group because all 18 components carry non-null values, so every AAPS group resolves to change or keep. Fourth, the earlier framing that the SMB minute caps are the effective safety cap is corrected: the caps compute correctly but are then multiplied by undocumented boost factors, so the cap is a base rather than a ceiling. Competing explanations for the same oscillation were compared. Unannounced meals driving unopposed rises is strongly supported by zero declared carbohydrate over 14 days and by cob 0 in every status, but it is an information problem rather than a parameter defect. Dynamic ISF overdosing at elevated glucose is quantitatively supported by variable_sens falling to 27.8 to 43 mg/dL/U above 170 mg/dL, but its factor is anchored to the flat profile ISF and the two cannot be separated in this package. Basal shape is weakened as described. DIA remains evidence-blocked without an insulin peak time or any uncontaminated decay window. Target behavior is confounded by an undocumented modulation producing 13 distinct target_bg values against three profile targets. The one finding that is both well evidenced and not entangled with any of these disputes is that the maximum IOB ceiling of 25 U never bound while observed IOB reached 5.935 U and predicted minGuardBG reached minus 59, so the last-resort brake is functionally absent during exactly the episodes that preceded the largest descents and the level 2 lows. Tightening that ceiling truncates only the extreme tail, does not alter ISF, basal, targets, SMB size or timing in ordinary operation, and therefore does not contaminate the attribution of any later change, which makes it the correct first step. The second-ranked change is aligning max_uam_smb_basal_minutes from 20 to 15 so the unannounced path is no longer permitted a larger base than the announced path; because the boosts are multiplicative, a 25 percent smaller base scales the boosted output proportionally. Everything else is held: all 17 profile rows keep, and AAPS groups 1, 2, 5 and 6 keep. The explicit revisit rule is that if the IOB brake and the UAM base alignment do not reduce the 18:00 to 19:00 and 00:00 to 03:00 local time below range, then either the dynamic ISF factor or the flat ISF anchor becomes the next candidate, and only one of the two may move.
analysis_steps.evidence: Full package cross-check against aaps_profile, profile_context and decision_inventory; iob 5.935 and 4.73 U against max_iob_units 25 U; minGuardBG minus 59 on 08-16 and minus 4 on 08-11; maxSafeBasal 4 derived from 0.8 U/h times max_daily_safety_multiplier 5.0; max_smb_basal_minutes 15 versus max_uam_smb_basal_minutes 20; SMB equals 1.6 against a nominal 0.167 U base on 08-19; hourly_glucose_local hours 4 to 8 clean versus hours 18, 19, 0 and 1 with high time below range; carb_entries 0 with cob 0 in all sampled statuses.
analysis_steps.dependencies: All eight preceding stages. The sequence constraint is that no two dependent insulin-delivery settings may move together, and the profile ISF anchor and the dynamic ISF factor may never be moved in the same cycle.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Boost multiplier configuration, insulin peak time, the custom target modulation rule, carbohydrate entries, rescue carbohydrate records, delivered basal volume, exercise data and itemized gap timestamps all remain unresolved, and each caps confidence in the areas being held rather than blocking the first two steps.

strengths.note: CGM coverage is 98.7 percent at a consistent 5-minute cadence with 3995 valid entries, zero invalid, zero duplicate and zero out-of-period readings, and a largest gap of only 65 minutes, which makes the dataset sufficient for every analysis stage.

Time in range of 86.0 percent and coefficient of variation of 32.6 percent both meet common consensus targets, indicating the overall therapy framework is working despite the specific overshoot pattern.

The local 04:00 to 08:00 fasting-like window is stable and clean, with means from 99.5 to 106.0 mg/dL, time in range from 95.2 to 98.7 percent and almost no time above range, which supports the current basal magnitude in the 00:00, 05:00 and 06:00 segments.

Loop-reported carb ratios match the profile segments in local time at 11.1, 13.2, 10.5 and 12.6 g/U, and the computed profile basal total of 16.2 U/day matches the profile switch label, which independently confirms the selected profile was the one running during the period.

Frequent 135 mg/dL temporary targets combined with smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled set to false form a deliberate and self-consistent defensive pattern that suppresses SMB when the user anticipates a fall.

Site changes, sensor changes, profile switches, GLP-1 doses and pump error events are all logged with timestamps, which allowed several glucose excursions to be attributed to hardware or medication context rather than misread as settings defects.

issues.note: Time below range is 5.1 percent, above the common reference of under 4 percent, with three level 2 events at 42, 41 and 42 mg/dL and hypoglycemia concentrated at local 19:00 with 15.3 percent and local 01:00 with 18.5 percent below range.

The maximum IOB ceiling of 25 U never bound during the period while observed IOB reached 5.935 U, roughly 17 percent of estimated daily dose, and predicted minGuardBG reached minus 59, meaning the last-resort brake was functionally absent during the episodes that preceded the largest glucose descents.

Configured SMB minute caps form only the base of the dose and are then scaled by undocumented boost factors, so a nominal 0.167 U base produced a delivered SMB of 1.6 U on 08-19, meaning the configured cap is not the effective delivery ceiling.

max_uam_smb_basal_minutes of 20 exceeds max_smb_basal_minutes of 15, so the less certain unannounced path is permitted a larger base dose than the announced path, while the announced path is never used because no carbohydrate is ever declared.

Zero carbohydrate entries were recorded over 14 days and cob was 0 in every sampled loop status, so all meal coverage runs reactively through UAM, producing unopposed rises at local 10:00 and across the 12:00 to 17:00 plateau followed by late over-correction.

Operational sensitivity from dynamic ISF ranges from 27.8 to 124.0 mg/dL/U against a flat profile anchor of 56 mg/dL/U, falling to roughly half the profile value at elevated glucose, which is the strongest candidate mechanism for the post-peak descents but cannot be separated from the profile ISF anchor in this package.

Sampled loop target_bg takes 13 distinct values from 80 to 116 mg/dL against three configured profile targets, with recurring 80 mg/dL targets during aggressive high-glucose episodes, while both autosens target flags are false and logged temporary targets explain only part of the spread, leaving the modulation rule undocumented.

DIA is 10 hours with insulin_type free_peak_oref and no insulin peak time supplied, and every post-bolus decay window is contaminated by subsequent SMB and temp basal activity, so DIA behavior cannot be evaluated from this dataset.

Several response windows show a crash followed by a large rebound, such as 47 mg/dL at 240 minutes then 204 mg/dL at 360 minutes on 08-13, which is consistent with unlogged rescue carbohydrate and means true time below range may be understated while some rebound highs are partly iatrogenic.

recommendations.title: Discuss tightening the maximum IOB ceiling as the single first change
recommendations.description: The configured maximum IOB of 25 U was never approached during the period while observed IOB reached 5.935 U on 08-21 and 4.73 U on 08-19, and both peaks immediately preceded the largest glucose descents of minus 176 and minus 168 mg/dL over six hours. Against an estimated total daily dose bracketed at 30 to 36 U per day, a 25 U ceiling represents roughly 70 to 80 percent of daily insulin and therefore provides no practical last-resort limit. Predicted minGuardBG reached minus 59 mg/dL on 08-16 and minus 4 mg/dL on 08-11 before 120-minute zero temps were issued, confirming the controller detects overshoot only after delivery has occurred. A ceiling near 8 U would have bound only in the two extreme episodes and would leave ordinary dosing untouched. This is the least entangled candidate in the package because it does not alter ISF, basal, targets, SMB size or SMB timing in normal operation and therefore does not contaminate attribution of any later change. The explicit trade-off to raise with the care team is that a binding ceiling will occasionally withhold correction of a genuine high, as would have occurred on 08-21 at 245 mg/dL with an insulin requirement of 2.12 U, which can extend time above range in those specific episodes.

observe: time below range at local hours 18, 19, 0, 1, 2 and 3
frequency of level 2 lows below 54 mg/dL
time above range at local hours 13 to 17 as the counter-effect

recommendations.title: Consider aligning the UAM SMB base with the announced SMB base only after the IOB ceiling has been observed
recommendations.description: max_uam_smb_basal_minutes of 20 currently exceeds max_smb_basal_minutes of 15, so the unannounced and less certain path is permitted a 33 percent larger base dose than the announced path, which is never used because no carbohydrate is ever declared. Because the boost factors observed in the reason strings are multiplicative, reducing the base by 25 percent scales the boosted output proportionally. This is placed second rather than first because it acts on the same insulin delivery pathway as the IOB ceiling, and moving both at once would make it impossible to attribute any change in evening or overnight time below range to either one. It should only be discussed after a full observation window on the first change.

suggested_change.prerequisite: complete one full observation window on the maximum IOB ceiling first
observe: time below range at local hours 18 and 19
size of post-peak descents in the afternoon
time above range at local hour 16

recommendations.title: Begin logging carbohydrate for one repeatable daily meal to unblock the largest number of held decisions
recommendations.description: Zero carbohydrate entries exist across 14 days and cob is 0 in every sampled loop status, which means carb ratio values of 13.2 g/U at local 08:00 and 10.5 g/U at local 16:00 have never been exercised, the carbohydrate absorption parameters have never been used, and no e-carb assessment is possible. Logging approximate grams with an accurate timestamp for the single most repeatable meal, the midday to afternoon eating that drives the local 12:00 to 17:00 plateau, for 10 to 14 consecutive days with no other change, would make carb ratio testable for the first time, populate COB so the absorption parameters become observable, produce the absorption curve needed to judge whether e-carbs fit that plateau, and separate the unannounced-meal explanation from the dynamic ISF and basal shape explanations that all three earlier stages had to defer. This is a data collection action rather than a therapy change and can proceed in parallel with the observation windows above.

suggested_change.to: approximate grams and accurate timestamp for one repeatable daily meal
observe: cob values appearing in loop statuses
glucose slope in the first 120 minutes after the logged meal
whether afternoon time above range falls without an increase in evening time below range

recommendations.title: Clarify the undocumented target modulation before any target discussion
recommendations.description: Configured profile targets are 90 mg/dL, 100 mg/dL from 08:00 and 90 mg/dL from 23:00, but sampled loop target_bg values include 80, 84, 86, 87, 90, 97, 99, 101, 104, 105, 106, 108 and 116 mg/dL, while autosens_raises_target and autosens_lowers_target are both false and the logged temporary targets at 135 and 108 mg/dL explain only part of that spread. The recurring 80 mg/dL targets appear specifically during the aggressive high-glucose episodes on 08-10, 08-18, 08-19 and 08-21. This is a customized AAPS build containing Enhanced oref1, UAM Boost, prTrial, twin and antBackout logic, so the modulation is most likely build-specific. This is best resolved by clarifying the plugin behavior rather than by any parameter change, and it caps confidence in every target-related decision until resolved.

suggested_change.to: documented plugin behavior confirmed by the user
observe: whether target_bg values reconcile with profile targets plus logged temporary targets once the rule is known

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep all 17 profile rows unchanged for now, including the seven basal segments, five carb ratios, the flat ISF of 56 mg/dL/U, the three targets and the 10-hour DIA, and direct the first change to the AAPS maximum IOB ceiling instead.
profile_recommendation.rationale: The only window plausibly free of both meals and residual correction insulin, local 04:00 to 08:00, is stable and well controlled with means from 99.5 to 106.0 mg/dL, time in range from 95.2 to 98.7 percent and essentially no time above range, which supports the current basal magnitude in the segments covering it. The afternoon and evening pattern does look phase-shifted, with the lowest daytime basal of 0.5 U/h at 16:00 coinciding with the day's highest hourly mean of 162.8 mg/dL and basal rising to 0.6 and 0.7 U/h into the highest hypoglycemia hours, but this cannot be attributed to basal because the evening and overnight hours show normal means alongside high time below range, which is the signature of residual insulin rather than an excessive baseline, and because repeated 120-minute zero temps show the controller braking against that residue. Three unresolved explanations remain entangled with the same evidence: zero declared carbohydrate over 14 days leaves unannounced meals fully plausible, dynamic ISF falling to 27.8 to 43 mg/dL/U at elevated glucose is a quantified alternative mechanism, and boost-scaled SMB delivering 1.6 U against a nominal 0.167 U base is a third. Changing any profile row now would confound the attribution of the safer, better-evidenced automation change and would risk shifting insulin rather than reducing it while time below range is already 5.1 percent with three level 2 events.
profile_recommendation.next_check: After one full 14-day observation window on the maximum IOB change alone, re-examine hourly_glucose_local for local hours 16 through 19 and 22 through 03; if time below range at local 19:00 falls from 15.3 percent and at local 01:00 falls from 18.5 percent while the local 16:00 peak of 162.8 mg/dL is unchanged, the residual-insulin explanation is confirmed and basal stays unchanged, whereas if the evening lows persist unchanged the 18:00 and 19:00 basal segments become the next candidate for a single small reduction.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: local hours 00 to 03 show means of 93.3, 90.6, 101.9 and 104.7 mg/dL, which are normal, alongside time below range of 11.4, 18.5, 10.1 and 10.2 percent. Normal means with high time below range indicate residual insulin action rather than an excessive baseline rate, because a genuinely over-set basal would depress the mean as well. Uncertainty: no per-hour IOB series exists to test the residual insulin hypothesis directly, and loop rate samples are too sparse to reconstruct delivered basal. Dependencies: the same overnight lows are candidate evidence for the 10-hour DIA tail, for boost-scaled evening SMB and for dynamic ISF, none of which are separated, so a basal reduction here could remove baseline insulin that is not the cause.

Evidence: local hour 05 shows a mean of 104.2 mg/dL with 95.2 percent time in range, 4.8 percent below range and zero time above range, which is within target. This falls inside the cleanest window of the dataset. Uncertainty: the 4.8 percent below-range figure is the highest in the 04:00 to 08:00 block and may reflect the tail of overnight residual insulin rather than this segment. Dependencies: none that would justify a change; any adjustment here should wait until the overnight residual insulin question is resolved by the maximum IOB observation window.

Evidence: local hours 06, 07 and 08 show means of 99.5, 99.5 and 110.5 mg/dL with time in range of 97.5, 98.7 and 98.2 percent, time below range of 2.5, 1.3 and 0.0 percent and time above range of 0.0, 0.0 and 1.8 percent. This is the best-controlled block in the entire period and is the strongest evidence in the package that basal magnitude is broadly appropriate. Uncertainty: the 42 mg/dL reading at 06:19 UTC on 08-21 falls in this window but occurred about 2.8 hours before a sensor change, so end-of-session inaccuracy is a live alternative explanation and it is not weighted as full evidence. Dependencies: none. This segment is the reference against which other windows are judged.

Evidence: local hour 10 has the second-highest daily mean at 148.0 mg/dL with 20.2 percent time above range and only 1.2 percent below range, following a climb from 110.5 at 08:00 and 132.9 at 09:00. Uncertainty: with zero carbohydrate entries across 14 days, an unannounced morning meal is at least as plausible an explanation as a basal shortfall, and the 08-14 window showing a rise of 88 mg/dL in 60 minutes from a starting value of 100 mg/dL has the shape of a meal rather than of insufficient baseline. Dependencies: raising basal here while time below range is 5.1 percent overall and while boost-scaled SMB delivery is unresolved would risk adding insulin to a system already reaching 5.935 U IOB. Carbohydrate logging is the prerequisite for evaluating this segment.

Evidence: local hour 16 carries the highest hourly mean of the day at 162.8 mg/dL with 32.1 percent time above range and zero percent below range, while this segment sets the lowest daytime basal rate, so the profile shape is inverted relative to the observed curve at this hour. Uncertainty: this hour sits at the peak of a broad 12:00 to 17:00 plateau with no discrete onset and zero declared carbohydrate, so unannounced afternoon eating is the leading explanation; separately, 180-minute temporary targets at 135 mg/dL on 08-17 and 08-18 deliberately suppressed SMB inside this window, meaning the same hourly statistic has at least two distinct causes on different days. Dependencies: this segment feeds directly into the 18:00 and 19:00 hypoglycemia cluster, so any increase here could deepen the largest existing safety problem. Carbohydrate logging must separate the causes first.

Evidence: local hour 18 shows 7.7 percent time below range with a minimum of 42 mg/dL and a falling mean of 124.2 mg/dL, and the profile raises basal from 0.5 to 0.6 U/h entering this hour, which is the direction opposite to the observed risk. Uncertainty: the descent into this hour is dominated by post-peak insulin arriving late, evidenced by 0.2 U at 234 mg/dL on 08-14 producing minus 178 mg/dL at 120 minutes, a drop the logged dose alone cannot produce, and by temp basal reaching the 4.0 U/h safe ceiling. A basal reduction of 0.1 U/h removes roughly 0.1 U per hour, which is negligible against boost-scaled SMB of 1.6 U. Dependencies: the maximum IOB change targets the same descent through a mechanism that matches its magnitude, and moving both would make attribution impossible. This segment becomes the next candidate only if the evening lows persist after that observation window.

Evidence: local hour 19 is the single worst hypoglycemia hour of the period at 15.3 percent time below range with a minimum of 41 mg/dL, and the profile raises basal again from 0.6 to 0.7 U/h entering it. Uncertainty: as with the 18:00 segment, the magnitude of the observed descents far exceeds what a 0.1 U/h basal difference could produce, and the two deepest level 2 clusters on 08-13 and 08-14 both followed large afternoon corrections rather than a steady baseline excess; 08-14 also had a GLP-1 dose that morning, which weakens it as evidence for any settings change. Dependencies: same as the 18:00 segment. Holding this row preserves clean attribution for the maximum IOB observation window, after which this segment and the 18:00 segment become the leading joint candidate for one small reduction, tested alone.

Evidence: no carbohydrate was declared at any point in the 14-day period, carb_entries is 0, total_carbs_g is 0.0 and cob was 0 in every sampled loop status, so this carb ratio has never been exercised and no observational basis exists to change it. A minor consistency observation is that loop reason strings report 13.3 g/U in this local segment against the profile value of 13.0, seen on 08-16 and 08-19, an offset of roughly 2 percent that may reflect dynamic carb ratio behavior, profile percentage or unit rounding. Uncertainty: that offset is small and its cause is not exposed in the package. Dependencies: carbohydrate logging is the prerequisite for evaluating any carb ratio; until then a change would be pure speculation.

Evidence: no carbohydrate was declared during the period, so this segment has never acted on a meal. The loop reason string on 08-09 at 03:01 UTC, which is 04:01 local, reports CR 11.1, matching the profile exactly and confirming the segment boundary is applied in local time. Uncertainty: consistency confirmation is not effectiveness validation; a matching value says nothing about whether 11.1 g/U doses a meal correctly. Dependencies: carbohydrate logging is required before any carb ratio can be assessed.

Evidence: this segment covers the mid-morning rise pattern where local hourly means climb from 110.5 at 08:00 to 148.0 at 10:00 with 20.2 percent time above range, but it is never invoked because carb_entries is 0, so those rises are handled entirely by UAM rather than by this carb ratio. Loop reason strings report CR 13.2 in this local window, matching the profile. Uncertainty: the morning rise could be caused by an unannounced meal, by the dawn-period basal, or by both, and these are not separated. Dependencies: carbohydrate logging for the morning meal is the prerequisite; this is the second-highest-value segment to validate after the afternoon one.

Evidence: this is the strongest carb ratio to have doses the afternoon plateau that peaks at local 16:00 with a mean of 162.8 mg/dL and 32.1 percent time above range, yet it is never invoked because no carbohydrate is declared. Loop reason strings report CR 10.5 in this local window, matching the profile. Uncertainty: because the plateau is slow and has no discrete onset, even a correct carb ratio would need appropriate meal timing to help, and no timing data exists. Dependencies: this is the single highest-value segment for the recommended carbohydrate logging, because validating it would simultaneously separate the unannounced-meal explanation from the dynamic ISF and basal shape explanations for the afternoon block.

Evidence: no carbohydrate was declared in this or any other window. Loop reason strings report CR 12.6 in this local segment, matching the profile. Local hours 20 and 21 are among the better-controlled evening hours with means of 117.0 and 120.0 mg/dL and time in range of 88.6 and 92.3 percent. Uncertainty: the absence of any exercised meal means the value is untested. Dependencies: carbohydrate logging is required before assessment; no evidence in this window suggests any problem.

Evidence: this flat single-segment value is not the sensitivity actually applied, because dynamic_sensitivity_enabled is true with an adjustment factor of 70 percent, and sampled variable_sens ranges from 27.8 to 124.0 mg/dL/U with a median near 79, falling monotonically as glucose rises. Uncertainty: the direction of any correction is genuinely ambiguous, since operational sensitivity is roughly half the profile value at high glucose and roughly double it at low glucose, so raising or lowering the anchor would help one end of the range and worsen the other. Dependencies: this is the critical one. Dynamic ISF is mathematically anchored to this value and to total daily dose, so the flat ISF and the 70 percent factor cannot be evaluated separately in this package and must never be moved in the same cycle. Moving this row now would also permanently confound the maximum IOB observation. If the first two changes do not reduce evening and overnight time below range, this row or the dynamic ISF factor becomes the next candidate, and only one of them may move.

Evidence: local hours 00 to 07 show acceptable means from 90.6 to 106.0 mg/dL, so the configured target is not producing elevated glucose, but time below range in hours 00 to 03 runs from 10.1 to 18.5 percent. Uncertainty: the configured value cannot be validated because sampled loop target_bg takes 13 distinct values from 80 to 116 mg/dL while both autosens target flags are false and logged temporary targets explain only part of the spread, meaning an undocumented build-specific mechanism is modulating the effective target. Dependencies: raising this target is a tempting response to the overnight lows, but the lows are better explained by residual insulin, and changing a target whose effective value is not reliably known would produce an uninterpretable result. The modulation rule should be clarified first.

Evidence: local hours 08 to 22 are covered by this segment and include both the best-controlled hour of the day at 08:00, with 98.2 percent time in range and zero percent below range, and the worst hyperglycemia block from 13:00 to 17:00. A single target cannot be blamed for both outcomes. Uncertainty: the same undocumented target modulation applies, and the recurring 80 mg/dL loop targets during the aggressive high-glucose episodes on 08-10, 08-18, 08-19 and 08-21 fall inside this segment, meaning the effective target during the riskiest moments is lower than configured for reasons not exposed in the package. Dependencies: clarification of the modulation rule is a prerequisite; until then any target change here has an unpredictable effective magnitude.

Evidence: local hour 23 shows a mean of 105.7 mg/dL with 88.7 percent time in range and 10.1 percent below range, so the mean is comfortable while the low exposure is elevated, which again matches residual insulin rather than a target that is set too low. Uncertainty: the undocumented target modulation applies here as it does to the other target rows. Dependencies: this row and the 00:00 target row govern the same overnight low cluster and would need to be considered together, which conflicts with the one-change-at-a-time rule while a better-matched and less entangled change, the maximum IOB ceiling, is available first.

Evidence: DIA is 10 hours with insulin_type free_peak_oref, and several response windows show effects persisting to 360 minutes, such as 0.05 U on 08-17 producing minus 34, minus 68 and minus 50 mg/dL at 2, 4 and 6 hours, and 08-19 showing minus 161 and minus 176 mg/dL at 4 and 6 hours. Uncertainty: this is evidence-blocked rather than merely uncertain. The insulin peak time is not supplied anywhere in the package, and every post-bolus decay window is contaminated by subsequent SMB delivery and temp basal activity, so it is impossible to determine whether the modelled tail is too fast or too slow relative to reality. Dependencies: DIA interacts with the 3-minute SMB interval and the multiplicative boosts to favour stacking, and peak IOB of 5.935 U is consistent with that interaction, but the maximum IOB ceiling addresses the same stacking risk with direct evidence. Changing DIA without a peak time and without one uncontaminated decay window would be speculative.

Evidence: both switches are enabled and consistent, and with carb_entries at 0 and cob at 0 in every sampled loop status, this pair is the only mechanism providing any meal coverage. Disabling either would remove all coverage of the local 13:00 to 17:00 block that reaches 32.1 percent time above range at 16:00. Aggregate outcomes of 86.0 percent time in range and 32.6 percent coefficient of variation indicate the framework itself is functioning. Uncertainty: the defect identified is dose magnitude from undocumented boost scaling, not the enable switches themselves. Dependencies: UAM is treated strictly as unannounced-rise detection and no duplicate COB counting is claimed, since cob is 0 throughout and no COB interaction is observable. Both source components carry non-null values, so verify is not admissible.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / SMB activation conditions (smb_always_enabled, smb_with_cob_enabled, smb_after_carbs_enabled, smb_with_temp_target_enabled, smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled)
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: the five flags are internally coherent. With smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled false, the frequent 135 mg/dL temporary targets logged on 08-09, 08-17, 08-18, 08-19 and 08-20 act as a deliberate SMB off-switch, which is a purposeful defensive pattern. Under smb_always_enabled true, the smb_with_cob_enabled and smb_after_carbs_enabled flags are effectively inert, and doubly so given zero carbohydrate entries. Uncertainty: the 180-minute temporary targets on 08-17 and 08-18 suppressed SMB across part of the afternoon peak window and may contribute to afternoon time above range, but 08-18 also had 12.8 percent time below range and followed a site change, so the effects are not separable. Dependencies: enabling smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled would increase hypoglycemia exposure against the binding 5.1 percent time below range constraint and is therefore not supported. All five components are non-null, so verify is not admissible.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / SMB strength and frequency (smb_interval_minutes, max_smb_basal_minutes, max_uam_smb_basal_minutes)
parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=15 min
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: the configured minute caps reconcile exactly with reported standardMaxBolus values, with 15 minutes against 0.7 to 0.8 U/h giving 0.175 to 0.20 U against a reported 0.2, and 20 minutes against 0.8 U/h giving 0.267 U against a reported 0.3. However these caps form only the base of the dose and are then multiplied by UAM Boost 1 between 0.68 and 1.34, UAM Boost 2 between 0.24 and 35.93, and a UAM High Boost path, so on 08-19 a nominal 0.167 U base against 0.5 U/h basal produced a stated SMB of 1.6 U. The specific inconsistency addressed here is that max_uam_smb_basal_minutes at 20 exceeds max_smb_basal_minutes at 15, permitting the less certain unannounced path a 33 percent larger base than the announced path, which is never used because no carbohydrate is declared. Aligning to 15 reduces the base by 25 percent and, because the boosts are multiplicative, scales boosted output proportionally. Uncertainty: if the true driver is dynamic ISF rather than the base, the reduction may be partially absorbed by larger boost factors and the effect may be small; the boost configuration itself is not exposed anywhere in the package. Dependencies: this acts on the same insulin delivery pathway as the maximum IOB ceiling, so it must follow a complete observation window on that change and must be moved alone. smb_interval_minutes is held at 3 as the configured minimum spacing, which was not confused with remaining-time text in reason strings, and no evidence isolates the interval as the driver. max_smb_basal_minutes is held at 15 as the reference the UAM path is being aligned to.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits (max_basal_u_per_hour, max_iob_units)
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: max_iob_units of 25 U never bound during the period. Peak observed IOB was 5.935 U on 08-21 with variable_sens at 27.8 mg/dL/U and an insulin requirement of 2.12 U at 245 mg/dL, and 4.73 U on 08-19 with a stated SMB of 1.6 U. Both peaks immediately preceded the largest descents in the dataset, minus 176 and minus 168 mg/dL over six hours, and predicted minGuardBG reached minus 59 mg/dL on 08-16 and minus 4 mg/dL on 08-11 before 120-minute zero temps were issued. Against an estimated total daily dose bracketed at 30 to 36 U per day, 25 U is roughly 70 to 80 percent of daily insulin, so the last-resort brake is functionally absent. A ceiling near 8 U, roughly 25 percent of estimated daily dose, would have bound only in the two extreme episodes. Uncertainty: the estimated daily dose is a bracket because delivered temp basal volume is not summarized in the package, so the exact ceiling value is a care-team decision rather than a derived number; the trade-off is that a binding ceiling will occasionally withhold correction of a genuine high and can extend time above range. Dependencies: max_basal_u_per_hour is held at 12 U/h because it is provably inert, since the 08-14 reason string shows the request reduced to maxSafeBasal 4, which equals the maximum profile basal of 0.8 U/h times the max_daily_safety_multiplier of 5.0, so the 12 U/h value has never been reached and changing it would have no effect. This change is placed first in the sequence precisely because it alters no ISF, basal, target, SMB size or SMB timing in normal operation and therefore does not contaminate attribution of any later change. Both components are non-null, so verify is not admissible.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / Autosens and Dynamic ISF (autosens_enabled, dynamic_sensitivity_enabled, autosens_raises_target, autosens_lowers_target, dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent)
parameter_decisions.rationale: Evidence: the combination is valid and non-conflicting, running one sensitivity engine rather than two, and both autosens target flags are consistently false with Autosens off. sensitivity_ratio is not stuck at 1, with observed values of 0.79, 0.88, 0.91, 0.92, 0.94, 0.98 and 1.0, confirming an active adjustment path where 1 is a neutral current adjustment rather than a disabled feature. This group is the strongest candidate mechanism for the crashes, because sampled variable_sens falls to 27.8 to 43.2 mg/dL/U above 170 mg/dL against a flat profile anchor of 56, driving insulin requirements of 1.98 to 2.59 U and rates to the 4.0 U/h ceiling. Uncertainty: the 70 percent factor is mathematically anchored to the profile ISF of 56 and to total daily dose, and the internal daily dose value used by the algorithm is not exposed, so the factor and the anchor cannot be evaluated separately within this package. Dependencies: changing the factor now would alter every dosing decision including the already hypoglycemia-prone overnight window and would permanently confound the profile ISF question that must still be resolved. The explicit revisit rule is that if the maximum IOB ceiling and the UAM base alignment do not reduce time below range at local hours 18, 19, 00 to 03, then either this factor or the profile ISF anchor becomes the next candidate, and only one of the two may move. All five components are non-null, so verify is not admissible.

Evidence: these two parameters govern COB decay and meal absorption modelling, and neither has been exercised once during the period. carb_entries is 0, total_carbs_g is 0.0, carb_treatment_entries is empty, extended_carb_entries is 0, average_extended_carb_duration_min is a genuine null, and cob is 0 in every sampled loop status. Uncertainty: there is no observational basis whatsoever to move either value, and no e-carb duration is inferred from any aggregate. Dependencies: these become tunable only once carbohydrate is declared, which is also the precondition for the meal strategy phase. A forward-looking feasibility note is that the configuration is already compatible with carbohydrate announcement, because smb_always_enabled true means SMB would continue regardless of COB, so smb_with_cob_enabled false and smb_after_carbs_enabled false would not block dosing, and min_carbs_required_grams of 20 would gate only the COB-dependent path. Both components are non-null, so verify is not admissible.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: The current approach is fully reactive: no prebolus, no immediate bolus fraction, no e-carbs, with SMB and UAM carrying one hundred percent of meal coverage. The most useful direction to discuss is not adding meal insulin but making the recurring midday to afternoon eating visible to the algorithm, by logging approximate carbohydrate grams with an accurate timestamp so the carb ratio of 10.5 g/U at local 16:00 can act proactively instead of UAM reacting late. Keep SMB and UAM enabled throughout, since they are the only current coverage and disabling either would remove all handling of the afternoon block. Hold prebolus timing and any immediate bolus percentage out of scope for now, because adding earlier insulin to a system that already reaches 5.935 U IOB and 41 mg/dL would move the same load earlier rather than reduce it until the IOB brake is in place. Hold e-carbs out of scope until ordinary carbohydrate entries have produced an observable absorption pattern, since an e-carb is a carbohydrate declaration spread over time that supplies COB and is not a pump extended bolus that spreads insulin.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: The user-declared analysis_context is source declared_by_user with meal_strategies as an empty list, period_exceptions null and strategy_stable_for_period null, so there is no declared prebolus, immediate bolus percentage or e-carb value in the package, and the stability rule cannot elevate any representative declaration; confidence is limited accordingly rather than any field being treated as contradicted. Observed telemetry is consistent with that empty declaration: 655 insulin entries totalling 275.95 U were delivered with zero declared grams, no Meal Bolus or Bolus Wizard event type appears anywhere, and every therapy response window is a Correction Bolus with is_extended_carbs false. Two recurring rise patterns are unopposed at onset and over-corrected afterwards. The mid-morning pattern climbs from 99.5 to 148.0 mg/dL between local 07:00 and 10:00, illustrated by 0.2 U at 100 mg/dL on 08-14 rising 88 mg/dL in 60 minutes and reaching 235 mg/dL at 240 minutes. The afternoon plateau runs 12:00 to 17:00 and peaks at 162.8 mg/dL with 32.1 percent above range, then falls to 105.4 mg/dL by 19:00 with 15.3 percent below range. Response windows show insulin arriving after the peak and persisting past the fall, with 0.2 U at 234 mg/dL producing minus 178 mg/dL at 120 minutes on 08-14, a magnitude the logged dose cannot produce and which matches boost-scaled UAM delivery plus temp basal at the 4.0 U/h ceiling. Several windows show crash then large rebound, such as 47 mg/dL at 240 minutes followed by 204 mg/dL at 360 minutes on 08-13, consistent with unlogged rescue carbohydrate.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log approximate carbohydrate grams with an accurate timestamp for the single most repeatable daily meal, the midday to afternoon eating that drives the local 12:00 to 17:00 plateau, for 10 to 14 consecutive days with no other setting changed, then check whether cob values appear in loop statuses and how glucose behaves in the first 120 minutes after each logged entry.

exceptions.pattern: Afternoon windows under a 135 mg/dL temporary target, including the 180-minute targets on 08-17 at 12:30 UTC and 08-18 at 14:24 UTC and shorter targets on 08-09, 08-19 and 08-20, all landing inside the 12:00 to 17:00 local plateau.
exceptions.suggestion: Treat elevated glucose during these specific windows as an intended trade-off rather than as evidence that the meal strategy or SMB settings are failing, and exclude these hours when judging whether any later change worked.
exceptions.rationale: With smb_with_high_temp_target_enabled set to false, these targets deliberately suppress SMB, visible as 126 mg/dL rising to 190 at 180 minutes on 08-17 and 185 falling only to 167 at 120 minutes on 08-18. The same afternoon time above range therefore has two distinct causes on different days, unopposed rises on most days and deliberate suppression on temporary target days, and conflating them would misattribute the result.

exceptions.pattern: Evening and overnight from local 22:00 to 03:00, where hourly means stay normal at 105.7, 93.3, 90.6, 101.9 and 104.7 mg/dL while time below range runs 6.6, 10.1, 11.4, 18.5 and 10.1 percent, with repeated 120-minute zero temps on 08-11, 08-16 and 08-20.
exceptions.suggestion: Exclude this window from meal strategy reasoning entirely and treat it as residual insulin from the afternoon rather than as a meal-related dosing error.
exceptions.rationale: There is no meal signature in this window, and normal means combined with high time below range is the signature of insulin residue rather than of mistimed or mis-sized meal insulin. Targeting it as a meal problem would produce the wrong change and would compete with the maximum IOB observation that addresses the same descent.

implementation_steps.title: Confirm the data foundation and the profile hold
implementation_steps.action: Review with the care team that CGM coverage of 98.7 percent over 14 days is adequate, that boundary days 2026-08-07 with 33 readings and 2026-08-21 with 269 readings are excluded from comparisons, and that all 17 profile rows are being held unchanged for this cycle. Note the confounders that must not be attributed to settings: the profile switch on 08-13, site changes on 08-10, 08-13 and 08-17, sensor changes on 08-11 and 08-21, the occlusion and pump error on 08-19, and GLP-1 doses on 08-14, 08-17 and 08-20.

implementation_steps.title: Discuss the maximum IOB ceiling as the single first change
implementation_steps.action: Discuss reducing max_iob_units from 25 U toward approximately 8 U, presenting the evidence that the ceiling never bound while observed IOB reached 5.935 U and predicted minGuardBG reached minus 59 mg/dL, and presenting the trade-off that a binding ceiling will occasionally withhold correction of a genuine high. Agree the exact value with the care team rather than adopting the illustrative figure. Change nothing else in this cycle.

implementation_steps.title: Observe for 14 days without any other change
implementation_steps.action: Track time below range at local hours 18, 19, 00, 01, 02 and 03, peak IOB per day, the count of readings below 54 mg/dL, and as the counter-effect, time above range at local hours 13 to 17 and the local 16:00 mean of 162.8 mg/dL. Keep making any temporary target entries as before so that behavior stays comparable.

implementation_steps.title: Begin carbohydrate logging for one meal in parallel
implementation_steps.action: Start logging approximate grams with an accurate timestamp for the single most repeatable daily meal that drives the local 12:00 to 17:00 plateau, for 10 to 14 consecutive days. This is data collection rather than a therapy change and may run alongside step 3, but no insulin setting should be altered because of it during this window.

implementation_steps.title: Reassess and, if supported, discuss the UAM SMB base alignment
implementation_steps.action: If evening and overnight time below range has not improved after step 3, discuss aligning max_uam_smb_basal_minutes from 20 min to 15 min so the unannounced path is no longer permitted a larger base than the announced path. Move this setting alone and observe for a further 14 days using the same metrics.

implementation_steps.title: Clarify the target modulation and the boost configuration
implementation_steps.action: Ask about the custom build behavior that produces 13 distinct loop target values from 80 to 116 mg/dL against three configured profile targets while both autosens target flags are false, and about where the UAM Boost 1, UAM Boost 2 and UAM High Boost factors are configured. Both are documentation questions, not changes, and both cap confidence in later decisions until answered.

implementation_steps.title: Only then revisit sensitivity or the ISF anchor, never both
implementation_steps.action: If the first two changes have not reduced time below range at local hours 18, 19 and 00 to 03, discuss either the dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent of 70 or the flat profile ISF of 56 mg/dL/U, choosing exactly one. These two are mathematically coupled and moving both in the same cycle would make the result uninterpretable. If instead the evening lows resolve but the local 18:00 and 19:00 hours remain the worst, the 18:00 and 19:00 basal segments become the next single candidate.
implementation_steps.change: none in this cycle; one candidate to be selected with the care team

education.note: When an hour shows a normal mean but high time below range, as local hours 00 to 03 do here with means from 90.6 to 104.7 mg/dL alongside 10.1 to 18.5 percent below range, that pattern usually points to insulin arriving from earlier activity rather than to a baseline rate that is set too high. A genuinely excessive baseline tends to pull the average down as well, so reading the mean and the low exposure together helps separate the two.

education.topic: Why a maximum IOB limit matters even when it seems generous
education.note: A maximum IOB setting is a last-resort brake rather than a routine dosing control. If it sits far above anything the system ever reaches, it never engages during exactly the episodes it exists to catch. Comparing the ceiling to observed peak IOB and to estimated total daily insulin is what shows whether the brake is doing anything at all.

Settings that limit micro-bolus size are expressed in minutes of basal, so the actual limit depends on the basal rate in force at that moment. In customized builds, that computed figure can be a starting point that other logic then scales, which is why comparing the setting to the dose actually delivered in the log is more informative than reading the setting alone.

education.topic: Dynamic sensitivity versus a fixed profile ISF
education.note: When dynamic sensitivity is active, the single ISF value in the profile acts as an anchor rather than as the number used for each decision. The effective figure changes with glucose, which is why one profile value can produce very different dosing behavior at high and low readings. Because the adjustment is calculated from the anchor, changing the anchor and the adjustment strength at the same time makes the result impossible to interpret.

education.topic: What unannounced meals do to a loop
education.note: Without carbohydrate entries the algorithm has no advance information and can only respond after glucose has already started rising. That produces a characteristic shape of a late peak followed by a delayed, larger correction, which is visible here as the local 16:00 peak followed by the 18:00 and 19:00 low cluster. Logging even approximate grams changes the algorithm from reacting to anticipating.

education.topic: Extended carbohydrate entries are not extended boluses
education.note: An extended carbohydrate entry declares carbohydrate spread over a period so the algorithm carries carbs on board and can dose ahead. A pump extended or dual-wave bolus spreads the insulin delivery instead. They solve different problems, and the first cannot be assessed at all without carbohydrate records to fit an absorption pattern against.

education.topic: Changing one setting at a time
education.note: Several settings here could each explain the same pattern, including basal shape, sensitivity, insulin duration and micro-bolus size. Moving more than one in the same period means any improvement or worsening cannot be attributed, so a slower sequence with a full observation window between changes usually yields more usable information than several simultaneous adjustments.

Site changes, sensor changes, occlusion or pump errors, and medication doses all shift glucose independently of any setting. In this period the worst day followed a site change, one high excursion followed a logged pump error, and one low preceded a sensor change by under three hours, so those readings carry less weight as evidence for any settings decision.

safety_notes: This is decision-support content only and is not medical advice. Every proposed change must be independently verified with your diabetes care team before anything is altered.
Do not change any AAPS setting automatically or as a result of this analysis alone. Make at most one change at a time and monitor glucose closely afterwards.

Time below range is 5.1 percent with three level 2 readings at 42, 41 and 42 mg/dL, which is the binding safety constraint. No change discussed here should increase insulin delivery in the evening or overnight windows.

The single change placed first is a reduction of the maximum IOB ceiling, which is a protective limit. Its trade-off is that it will occasionally withhold correction of a genuine high and may extend time above range in those specific episodes, so discuss that trade-off explicitly.
Profile ISF and the dynamic ISF adjustment factor are mathematically coupled. They must never be changed in the same cycle, and neither should be changed until the earlier steps have been observed.

This is a customized AAPS build containing boost logic and target modulation that are not exposed in the supplied settings, so observed behavior may differ from what the listed values suggest. Confirm the actual behavior of your build before relying on any inference here.

Several glucose excursions coincide with a pump occlusion and error on 08-19, site changes on 08-10, 08-13 and 08-17, sensor changes on 08-11 and 08-21, and GLP-1 doses on 08-14, 08-17 and 08-20. These should not be treated as evidence of a settings problem.

Repeated crash and rebound patterns suggest hypoglycemia treatments may not have been recorded, which means true time below range could be understated. Recording rescue carbohydrate would improve the safety picture significantly.

Continue to keep fast-acting carbohydrate available, particularly in the local 18:00 to 19:00 and overnight windows where the deepest lows occurred, and contact your care team promptly about any severe or unexplained hypoglycemia.
